CONCLUDED 2026-09-05 (KEEP, live). ACTIVATED + SHIPPED 2026-09-02 (commit 2f469fa). Loop-side code only -- live on the NEXT nightgate invocation, no camera restart and no env delta. The loop could not report its own death: loop.nightgate heartbeats ONLY on gated-out ticks, so (a) a tick that PASSES the gate and then dies is completely silent -- the 27-night OAuth outage 2026-08-04..29, found only because Daniel looked -- and (b) nothing checks the camera at all, so the ~20h manual-stop outage 2026-09-01 19:13 -> 09-02 15:14 was silent too. Fix: two independent best-effort checks in nightgate, run on EVERY tick (proceed or skip -- the outage was on PASSING ticks, so a skip-only check would have missed it): loop staleness (days_behind(last_tick_completed_day, loop_day()) > 2 -> alert, stamped once per loop-day in last_staleness_alert_loopday; threshold 2 not 1 so a single normal missed night never pages) and camera liveness (systemctl is-active wildlife-camera.service != active -> alert, stamped in last_camera_alert_loopday). Both wrapped in try/except that logs and continues: neither can change the gate's exit code or raise out of main(), so a broken alert path degrades to the OLD behaviour (silence), never to a broken gate -- the key constraint, since nightgate is the one component whose death silences everything downstream. Decision logic is 3 pure functions (days_behind, should_alert_staleness, should_alert_camera_down) tested without I/O. 550 tests pass (was 532). Replayed against both real incidents: both fire. Live smoke test on a copy of real state: proceeds, exit 0, no alert, no Telegram -- state is exactly 2 days behind and '>2' is correctly false at the boundary. FN-veto N/A (touches no detection/classification/mute/routing path). RESIDUAL GAP, not solved: the switch lives INSIDE nightgate, so it cannot fire if the timer itself stops -- and the 2026-09-01 tick never ran at all. That needs an off-Pi watchdog and is explicitly not claimed here. Rollback: git revert 2f469fa, no restart. See runs/0013. REJECTED AS DESIGNED 2026-09-02 -- the pre-registered fix was re-measured before shipping, as the protocol requires, and the measurement REFUTED it. Do not re-derive it. The release trigger opened on 08-31 ('ship as the first act of the tick that concludes exp #14') fired on this tick and was correctly spent on re-validation, not on shipping. Pre-registered design was a score floor on the human gate's homo-taxon arm (SPECIES_HOMO_TAXON_MIN_SCORE=0.75), sited in what night 1 read as an empty trough between an 'adjudicated-empty' low mode (<=0.66, 17/17 bursts empty) and a 'confirmed-people' high mode (>=0.85). The 09-01/02 window contains 34 taxon-arm HUMAN rows with pc<0.50, 17 of them low-mode, ALL 17 with frames on disk and ALL 17 adjudicated: SIX CONTAIN REAL PEOPLE -- 4907 (0.549), 4840 (0.599), 4897 (0.617), 4845 (0.631), 4850 (0.673), 4848 (0.674); 4840/4848 show two adults full-frame and plainly identifiable. Empties occupy 0.579-0.731, people occupy 0.549-0.674: the two classes are COMPLETELY INTERLEAVED and no in-BOUNDS floor separates them. Night 1's bimodality was a sampling artifact of a quiet day with almost no human traffic, not a property of the signal. Counterfactual over the window: 4897 (person at close range, 2186s after the previous surviving HUMAN burst, density 0, no HUMAN burst inside the 240s deferral) would have been SENT TO REVIEW -- every layer of the proximity/density/deferral stack is blind to it. That is a rollback event under exp #14's own standing rule, so it must not be deployed in the first place. WHAT SURVIVES: the phantom half of the finding is confirmed and strengthened -- 11 of 17 low-mode taxon rows are empty garden and they do arm real mutes (4828 armed two; 3 of 9 proximity mutes in the window were phantom-armed). WHAT IS REFUTED: that the ensemble's homo-taxon score can tell people from empty scenes. Any future attempt needs a DIFFERENT DISCRIMINATOR, not a different threshold. Absent one the taxon arm stays unthresholded, because the failure mode of leaving it alone (a muted empty scene, costing observability) is strictly cheaper than the failure mode of demoting it (a person's photo in REVIEW). See runs/0012 'Backlog #16 ... REFUTED'.

ACTIVATED + SHIPPED 2026-09-09 (commit f73a8ae, restart-gated 09-10T03:25). The human/privacy gate evaluates exactly ONE frame per burst — the sharpest — and sharpness is uncorrelated with whether a person is visible, so a burst can leak a person the gate never scored. Burst 5119 leaked a recognisable child's face: frames 1-4 classify human (pc 0.89 on two), only frame5 does not, and frame5 won selection by 13.57 vs 13.41. Burst 5096 the same morning is a second instance. Threshold measured over 142 on-disk review-class bursts: the 2 person-carrying ones ranked 1-2 at 0.169/0.215, busiest empty burst 0.082. Prediction: <=1 person-in-non-selected-frame burst reaches REVIEW per night; sweep fires on ~10% of review-class bursts. Rollback: PERFORMANCE_HUMAN_SWEEP_DIVERGENCE_THRESHOLD=0.

OPENED 2026-09-23. loop.metrics counts person-labelled rows in the labeled_triggers denominator but never in fp_count, so a person-heavy night prints a flatteringly low fp_rate into metrics/daily.csv. 2026-09-23 is the first severe case: 32 triggers, 29 of them person, fp_rate 0.094 vs 0.286 the night before — an apparent 3x improvement that is entirely composition, not behaviour. The honest statement was '3 non-person triggers, 3 false positives, 0 animals'. Risk is self-poisoning: a future tick reads the dip as an FP win and credits whatever shipped that day. Candidate fix: exclude person-labelled rows from the fp_rate denominator the same way n_cant_tell and n_sampled_out already are, and surface them as their own report line (n_person). Cheap, no new data needed — the labels are already in detection_feedback. Not shipped 2026-09-23 (one change per tick; exp #35 took it).

nightly_verdict: Quiet night for wildlife: 32 triggers, no animals, and for the first time not a single alert needed to reach you — a long gardening session plus three empty-garden false alarms, all correctly silenced. I found and fixed a privacy bug while checking them: one close-up photo of a person had been correctly hidden from you but was not being deleted on the 48-hour schedule, and 12 such bursts have slipped through since July.
